subject: Update to Commit/Best Case definitions and drop-in clinics
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sales Leadership <sales-leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Update to Commit/Best Case definitions and drop-in clinics

Team,

Quick heads up: we've finalized a short set of definition changes to make Commit vs Best Case more objective and easier to audit during weekly forecast reviews. The goal is to reduce subjectivity and improve forecast accuracy while keeping seller motion straightforward. Highlights (full playbook attached):

- Commit: requires a signed PO/contract OR a documented, confirmed legal approval + finance billing cadence established.
- Best Case: active procurement or legal review but no signed instrument; high likelihood but not yet committed to revenue recognition.
- Pipeline (all other stages): opportunities without immediate procurement/legal evidence or too early in discovery.

Timeline and asks:
- Please update any outstanding deals that you would have historically called Commit by end-of-day 2028-07-25.
- Weekly forecast snapshots starting 2028-07-28 will reflect the new categories.
- We’re running 30-minute drop-in clinics next week (no slide marathon) to walk edge cases and show the sandbox tooling. RSVP to the slot that works for you.

Attachments: commit-playbook-v2.pdf, quick-change-checklist.xlsx.

If you have specific deals you want us to triage, paste the HubSpot link in your RSVP and we’ll look during the clinic.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Update to Commit/Best Case definitions and drop-in clinics

Thanks, Lauren — quick clarification: for Dedicated deals where procurement has already raised a PO request but finance hasn’t issued a billing schedule (PO pending finance review), do we treat those as Best Case until the PO is complete? I have a handful of accounts in that exact state (see https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/2048) and want to make sure we apply the change consistently.

Also: will Ops run a one-time script to flag deals where current stage conflicts with new definitions? That would speed cleanup.

— Vivek

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Update to Commit/Best Case definitions and drop-in clinics

Vivek — good question. Short answer: leave as Best Case until we have either the signed PO or a finance-billing cadence confirmed in writing. Operationally:

1) Sellers should add a short note in HubSpot (deal -> Internal Notes) linking the procurement PR/PO ticket and expected sign date.
2) If there’s a formal procurement acknowledgement but finance hasn’t completed billing setup, mark as Best Case and tag "Awaiting billing".
3) Ops will run a reconciler script after EOD 2028-07-25 to surface mismatches; Lauren, can we turn that on?

This keeps the definition clean and gives us auditability.

Karthik
Director, Forecast Ops

From: Samantha Reyes <samantha@foresight.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Question on partner-sourced deals and Commit criteria

Hi Lauren — thanks for the heads up. For partner-sourced transactions (we bring the buyer, Redwood invoices), how should our team annotate those in HubSpot when we have a signed referral agreement but not the end-customer PO yet? Our finance team wants to ensure partner revenue sits in the right bucket for forecasting.

Samantha Reyes
Partnerships Lead, Foresight Analytics
Samantha@foresight.ai

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Reyes <samantha@foresight.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on partner-sourced deals and Commit criteria

Samantha — good question. Short guidance: partner-sourced deals follow the same Commit vs Best Case rules. A signed referral agreement alone does not constitute Commit for the end-customer revenue — we need either the customer PO signed to Redwood or a documented, signed commercial instrument that authorizes Redwood to invoice.

For edge cases where the partner agreement includes explicit assignment/authorization language, please attach that document to the HubSpot deal and tag it "Partner: Authorization". If you want, bring a live deal to one of our drop-in clinics and we’ll triage it with Finance so the revenue recognition folks are comfortable.

If Acme Procurement needs a one-off exception, have them file a request to finance@redwood.ai and include the relevant docs.

— Lauren
Head of Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
